minutes.headline: ZBA voted to grant a variance letting a modular food pantry building be placed at 30 School Street.
minutes.summary: The board heard the planning director preview four 2027 zoning amendments, then held a variance hearing for a one-story manufactured building to house the Lunenburg food pantry in the village center district. After debate over alternatives, the timing and the building's appearance, the board approved the variance and waived the application fees.

budget_items.topic: Cost of a permanent food pantry building
budget_items.what_was_said: The pantry president said a permanent building would cost far more than it could raise, which is why a temporary modular unit is proposed.
The planning director said full site plan review requires an engineered plan that is expensive and slow, and a minor review would spare simple reuse projects that cost.
The pantry is negotiating a license with the town for the site and must restore the land, removing the pad, when it leaves.

decisions.decision: The planning director asked boards to send comments on the draft zoning amendments by the end of November; a board member will send him material on using 'shall' rather than 'should'.
The variance was approved; the chair read standard post-decision conditions and appeal and filing timelines.
A member offered to arrange a discussion with the Parks Commission about the back section of Wallace Park as an alternative site if other options fail.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to grant a variance for a one-story modular building to house the Lunenburg food pantry at 30 School Street.
The board also voted by voice to waive the application fees for the food pantry.
The chair read the standard post-decision conditions and the appeal and filing timelines after the variance passed.
A member offered to arrange a talk with the Parks Commission about the back of Wallace Park as an alternative site if other options fail.
The planning director previewed four 2027 zoning amendments and asked boards for comments by the end of November.

why_it_matters: The decision lets the food pantry put a temporary building in the village center, with the site still subject to a license being negotiated with the town and a duty to restore the land when it leaves.

The proposed 2027 zoning amendments on senior, inclusionary and cluster housing and on minor site plan review could change how projects are approved, and residents may be asked to vote on them at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Comments on the draft 2027 zoning amendments are due to the planning director by the end of November.
The pantry's license with the town for the 30 School Street site, still under negotiation, and the appeal window the chair read after the decision.
